prerequisite: census timing audit establishing that some island-year colony rows are collected on multiple dates
question: Can the positive within-island colony-growth synchrony contrast survive when shared same-day census batches are removed from the pairwise growth observations?

data.missingness: retain only observed adjacent-year growth intervals; no missing-as-zero and no identifier merging

primary_strict.interval_rule: for a pair of colony codes, retain an annual growth interval only if the two colonies were counted on different dates at both the start year and the end year
primary_strict.minimum_overlap: at least 4 retained intervals, giving positive Fisher-z information weight n-3
primary_strict.statistic: same Fisher-z information-weighted within-island minus between-island growth-correlation contrast used in overlap V1
primary_strict.null: permute island labels within five fixed mean-log1p-abundance rank strata while trajectories, dates and missingness remain attached to colony units
primary_strict.decision: support against exact same-day batch confounding only if the strict estimator is valid and its two-sided permutation p <= 0.05

relaxed_diagnostic.interval_rule: retain intervals where census dates differ at at least one endpoint
relaxed_diagnostic.role: descriptive sensitivity only; cannot by itself rule out a same-day error contribution at the other endpoint

boundaries: This test addresses exact same-date batching only, not observer identity, protocol-level error, or island-wide biological/environmental shocks.
If the strict estimator has inadequate information, report it as inconclusive rather than relax the primary rule.
Do not change the 4-interval minimum, date rule, Fisher weighting, abundance strata, transform, or permutation scheme after opening the result.
